'''Tom Okia Okurut''' (6 January 1960 – 14 April 2024) was a [[Uganda]]n [[climate change activist]], conservationist, [[environmentalist]], author, and policy maker.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |title=Agriculture ministry, NEMA mourn climate change icon |url=https://www.newvision.co.ug/articledetails/NV_186285 |access-date=2024-05-30 |website=New Vision |date=19 April 2024 }}</ref><ref name=":6">{{Cite web |date=2023-10-22 |title=Experts urge farmers to embrace one-acre model farming |url=https://www.kfm.co.ug/news/experts-urge-farmers-to-embrace-one-acre-model-farming.html |access-date=2024-05-31 |website=93.3 KFM }}</ref> He was the former executive director [[National Environment Management Authority of Uganda|National Environment Management Authority]] for 10 years since 2011 to 2021,<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2024-04-14 |title=Former NEMA boss, Dr Tom Okurut dies after brain surgery |url=https://www.monitor.co.ug/uganda/news/national/former-nema-boss-dr-tom-okurut-dies-after-brain-surgery-4590530 |access-date=2024-05-30 |website=Monitor }}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Former NEMA boss Dr Okurut dead |url=https://www.newvision.co.ug/articledetails/NV_185877 |access-date=2024-05-30 |website=New Vision |date=14 April 2024 }}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |date=2024-04-15 |title=Ex NEMA Boss Dr Tom Okurut Succumbs to Brain Clot |url=https://chimpreports.com/ex-nema-boss-dr-tom-okurut-succumbs-to-brain-clot/ |access-date=2024-05-30 |website=ChimpReports }}</ref><ref name=":4">{{Cite web |last=apofeed |date=2024-04-18 |title=Uganda: Plant trees in memory of fallen Ex - National Environment Management Authority (NEMA) Boss, Among urges public |url=https://african.business/2024/04/apo-newsfeed/uganda-plant-trees-in-memory-of-fallen-ex-national-environment-management-authority-nema-boss-among-urges-public |access-date=2024-05-30 |website=African Business }}</ref> and former executive director Climate Change Action East Africa.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=IHE Delft alumnus Tom Okurut Okia passes away |url=https://www.un-ihe.org/news/ihe-delft-alumnus-tom-okurut-okia-dies |access-date=2024-05-30 |website=www.un-ihe.org |date=18 April 2024 }}</ref><ref name=":5" /><ref name=":6" />

== Background and Education ==
Okurut attended Akadot Primary School from 1967 to 1973, Gulu High School between 1974 and 1977, [[Teso College Aloet]] from 1978 up to 1979.<ref name=":5" /> Okurut joined Makerere University in 1980 and graduated with a bachelor's degree of science majoring in chemistry in 1983.<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":6" /> He obtained a post graduate diploma in renewable engineering from [[Urbino University|Eni-Sogesta Institute Urbino]] in Italy.<ref name=":5" /> Between 1987 up to 1988, he pursued his [[Master of Science]] at University of Ibadan in Nigeria,<ref name=":5" /> and he also attended [[IHE Delft Institute for Water Education]] in Netherlands where he did his PhD in Environmental Science and Technology from 1995 to 2000.<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":6" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" />

Okurut died on 14 April 2024 at Platinum Hospital in [[Nakasero]], Kampala due to head clot that had reached his brain which prompted a head surgery.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /><ref name=":4" /><ref name=":7">{{Cite web |last=Enuru |first=Eddy |date=2024-04-15 |title=Former NEMA Executive Director Dr. Tom Okurut, dies |url=https://nilepost.co.ug/news/195659/former-nema-executive-director-dr-tom-okurut-dies |access-date=2024-05-31 |website=Nilepost News }}</ref> He died in the Intensive Care Unit due to alleged lack of oxygen circulation in the brain after the head surgery.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Gapany |first=M. |date=January 2007 |title=Is Lack of Placement of Drains After Thyroidectomy With Central Neck Dissection Safe? A Prospective, Randomized Study |url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1016/s1041-892x(07)70194-4 |journal=Yearbook of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery |volume=2007 |pages=227–228 |doi=10.1016/s1041-892x(07)70194-4 |issn=1041-892X|url-access=subscription }}</ref> He was buried on 20 April 2024 in Akadot village, Mukongoro subcounty in [[Kumi District|Kumi district]].<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":6" /><ref name=":4" />

== Personal life ==
Okurut was married to Ademun Anna Rose Okurut who serves as the Commissioner of Animal Health at the [[Ministry of Agriculture, Animal Industry and Fisheries (Uganda)|Ministry of Agriculture, Animal Industry and Fisheries]]. They had 3 children.<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":3" />

== Career ==
Okurut started his career as an assistant lecturer in the chemistry department at Makerere University from 1989 to 1994 after his first degree.<ref name=":5" /> He joined National Water and Sewage Corporation in 2000 as a Water quality officer  up to 2001 in the quality, training, research and development department<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":2" /> and he was the executive secretary for the lake Victoria Basin Commission in Kisumu, Kenya from 2006 to 2011 and he was promoted to program officer at the Lake Victoria development program, [[East African Community]] secretariat which is based in Arusha, Tanzania.<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":1" />

Okurut was appointed the executive director of NEMA<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-01-15 |title=One year later, Kilembe mines is yet to reopen |url=https://www.monitor.co.ug/uganda/news/national/one-year-later-kilembe-mines-is-yet-to-reopen-1682830 |access-date=2024-05-31 |website=Monitor }}</ref> in 2011 up to 1 September 2021 when he was succeeded by Akankwasah Barirega after serving two regimes.<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":7" /> While at NEMA, it is alleged that he contributed to the entity success story where the entity managed to earn 500% budget increment and 100% in 5-years, lowered the pollution rate to 50% as a result of engineering innovative compliance assistant strategy, he called for the development of national guidelines and standards for workplace air quality and drafted the financial law for single plastic usage.<ref name=":2" />

Okurut was the executive director of Climate Change Action for East Africa from 2021 till his death on 14 April 2024.<ref name=":5" />

Okurut served as the chairperson on the Appointment Board and Council member of [[Makerere University Business School]].<ref name=":2" />

== Honor ==
In honor of Okurut's work, [[Anita Among]] requested the member of parliament to plant a minimum of five trees.<ref name=":4" />

== Awards ==
Okurut was the receiver of the UNESCO - IHE Alumni award 2014 which is given to alumni of IHE Delft who have contributed exceptionally to the water management and his service as a role model to fellow water professionals.<ref>[https://ihe-delft-ihe-website-production.s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2024-04/update_dec2014e.pdf MAGAZINE UNESCO‑IHE INSTITUTE FOR WATER EDUCATION - 2014]</ref>
